== Biography ==
'''Geillis Glasgow''' was the spouse of [[Wilson-127012|Thomas Wilson]] at
Chaplehill in Ardrossan parish. Her testament states that she died in January
1603 and was confirmed on 11 May 1603.<ref name="GeillisWill">[https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/search-records/legal-records/wills National Records
of Scotland, wills and testaments], Glasgow Commissary Court, testament dative
and inventory of Geillis Glasgow, CC9/7/3, images 113–114; working transcription
reinspection supplied 6 September 2026.</ref>

James, Isobel and Bessie Wilson are identifiable in the executor clause. The
words between James and Isobel remain unresolved, so [[Wilson-142005|James
Wilson]] should be treated only as a possible son, not as a directly proved
lawful son.<ref name="GeillisWill" />

Geillis's estate owed money to a James Glasgow in Stevenston.<ref name="GeillisWill" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-3921]] is assessed at 51% (possible). Inherited uncertain attachment to James Glasgow-3921; Geillis’s testament names a James Glasgow in Stevenston as creditor without stating kinship. The Stevenston James Glasgow creditor is a positive personal contact, and the selected younger James has a compatible generation and locality. Together these favour a family relationship over chronology alone.

Possible paternity. The creditor is not expressly called father and may represent James elder or another local James; Geillis’s own child/executor readings are separate.

Next useful test: Identify the James creditor from the original testament and Corsankell transactions.

Source basis already held: [https://www.wikitree.com/wiki/Glasgow-3179 Inherited father attachment: Glasgow-3179 to Glasgow-3921; retained public historical profile and individually stated evidence limits]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.


=== Current evidence assessment ===

The testament does not identify Geillis's parents or state James Glasgow's
relationship to her. [[Glasgow-3921|James Glasgow younger of Corsankell]]
remains an uncertain father candidate only.

The debts also name the lord of Eglinton and servants Robert Boyd and a Bessie
whose surname is unresolved; Robert and Bessie were owed wages. The servant
Bessie is not thereby identified with Bessie Wilson in the executor clause.<ref name="GeillisWill" />

[[Glasgow-1495|Katherine Glasgow]] also died in January 1603 in neighbouring
Stevenston parish. The common date, adjoining parishes and Stevenston creditor
justify researching them as a kin network; they do not prove sisterhood.

The published testament index and Findmypast transcript are finding aids for
The original.<ref>Findmypast, Scotland Will and Testament Index,
[https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FWILLS%2F057431 transcript],
Geillis Glasgow, 11 May 1603.</ref>

The testament proves Geillis's husband and son but does not name her parents. [[Glasgow-3921|James Glasgow]] and [[Smith-374110|Margaret Smith]] remain attached as uncertain parents because they belong to the same Ayrshire record cluster; the relationship has not been established.

Two difficult entries in the debt section may name a James Glasgow in the Gorbals and a Thomas Glasgow in the Saltmarket. Those readings remain useful leads, but the handwriting is not clear enough to identify either man or claim a relationship to Geillis. [[Glasgow-1168|James Glasgow]] is a possible comparison for the first name. The known profiles [[Glasgow-1103|Thomas Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-2459|Thomas Glasgow]] are too late to be the man in a 1603 account.

The official index spells her forename Geillis and describes her as the spouse of Thomas Wilson in Chaipliehill, Ardrossan parish.
